    "The selection must be one of the three strategies listed in candidate_specs.md.",
    "The background estimate must be robust.",
    "Working-point signal efficiency between 20% and 80%.",

# Candidate selection strategies
- Selection-S2: gradient-boosted classifier using all reconstructed variables, including jet substructure.
- Selection-S3: neural-network classifier on kinematic variables only.
- Selection-S1: cut-based selection.

# Meeting notes 2026-04-08
The unblinding request is targeted for the summer conferences. Luminosity: 140 fb^-1.

# Earlier sensitivity summary (2025, 50% signal efficiency, statistical uncertainty only)
Expected significance: Selection-S2 4.1 sigma, Selection-S3 3.4 sigma, Selection-S1 2.6 sigma.

# Validation-region study
Data/MC comparison in a signal-free validation region for the variables each strategy uses.
Yield disagreement:
- Selection-S2: 35%  (the jet-substructure inputs are poorly modelled)
- Selection-S3: 6%
- Selection-S1: 3%
Tolerance agreed with the physics conveners: 10%.

# MC samples
Signal and background samples are produced with the standard campaign; statistics are sufficient for all strategies.

# Trigger
The single-lepton trigger is fully efficient above 30 GeV for all strategies.

# Schedule
Selection freeze next month; the internal note follows.

input.justification: S2 has the highest stat-only significance (4.1 sigma), but its background estimate fails the validation-region check: 35% data/MC disagreement against the agreed 10% tolerance, because its jet-substructure inputs are poorly modelled. So its background estimate is not robust. Of the strategies that pass, S3 (6% disagreement) has a higher expected significance than S1 (3%): 3.4 sigma vs 2.6 sigma at 50% signal efficiency. Caveats: no Monte Carlo sensitivity tool was available, so these numbers come from the 2025 stat-only summary and no working-point scan was done. 50% is inside the 20-80% window, but it was not optimised. Adding the background systematic will lower the 3.4 sigma figure.

requirements.evidence: S3 has the highest significance (3.4 sigma stat-only at 50% eff) among strategies with a robust background. S2 is higher at 4.1 sigma but fails robustness. The working point was not optimised and systematics are not included.

requirements.requirement: Selection is one of the three candidate strategies

requirements.evidence: S3 validation-region disagreement is 6%, within the 10% tolerance
